correctness.rationale: If the first forced vertex lies on one side, its opposite side already displays exactly two colours. Any uncoloured vertex on that opposite side could never subsequently see two colours because properness restricts every coloured vertex on the first side to the unique third colour; therefore the opposite side must have been fully coloured initially. This yields the two symmetric non-total classes. Every total proper three-colouring has side colour-use pattern (2,1), (1,2), or (1,1), with the first two already counted and the last contributing six assignments. Direct independent enumeration for all 1<=m,n<=3 matched the closed coefficient formula exactly, including K1,2=6p^2(1-p).
